page: Amazon Web Services hpc7a.24xlarge is a dedicated High Performance Computing server built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance features 48 physical AMD EPYC 9R14 cores with x86_64 architecture running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz, operating with one thread per core to eliminate hyperthreading contention. Core instruction capabilities include extended vector extensions such as AVX-512, VAES, and SHA_NI. The system is provisioned with 768 GB of 5 GHz DDR5 memory, yielding 16 GB of memory per physical core. Network connectivity reaches a 150 Gbps baseline bandwidth. The server contains zero local ephemeral storage and no dedicated GPU hardware.

In benchmark evaluations, the hpc7a.24xlarge demonstrates top-tier multi-core processing performance. Multi-core stress-ng tests, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and software compilation via Clang in Geekbench all rank in the top 10 percent of recorded server benchmarks. The DDR5 memory subsystem achieves 695.05 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth and 347.3 GB/sec write bandwidth, alongside high throughput in PassMark physics simulations and Redis SET operations reaching 122.53 million operations per second. Single-threaded metrics, including static web serving and gzip compression, perform at average tier levels relative to the benchmark pool.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the architecture maximizes per-core throughput by provisioning 16 GB of high-frequency DDR5 RAM per physical CPU core, reducing memory contention in data-heavy tasks. The 150 Gbps network interface enables efficient scale-out cluster topologies without inter-node throughput constraints. Tradeoffs include the total absence of integrated local ephemeral storage, which requires reliance on network-attached storage, and the lack of discrete GPUs, making it unsuited for hardware-accelerated deep learning models.

The hpc7a.24xlarge is designed specifically for compute-heavy and bandwidth-intensive engineering and scientific workloads. Optimal applications include computational fluid dynamics, weather forecasting, molecular dynamics simulations, massive software build farms, parallelized financial modeling, and high-throughput memory-resident database engines.
description: Amazon Web Services hpc7a.24xlarge is a high-performance computing server equipped with 48 physical AMD EPYC 9R14 cores operating at 3.7 GHz, paired with 768 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 5 GHz. Running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it features 150 Gbps baseline networking bandwidth without hyperthreading or onboard local storage. Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier multi-core CPU scaling, high uncached memory bandwidth exceeding 695 GB/sec, and excellent software compilation performance. The instance delivers high resource density for parallel compute tasks that benefit from 16 GB of high-speed memory per physical core. However, the lack of local ephemeral NVMe storage and dedicated GPU accelerators requires relying on network storage solutions and limits its suitability for GPU-bound machine learning tasks. Overall, hpc7a.24xlarge is optimized for High Performance Computing (HPC) applications, computational fluid dynamics, large software build pipelines, and memory-bound distributed processing.
